identity.title: ALMA-IMF. V. Prestellar and protostellar core populations in the W43 cloud complex

paper_type_evidence.quote: We aim to compare populations of protostellar and prestellar cores in three regions imaged in the ALMA-IMF Large Program.

The study presented in this article is carried out in the context of the ALMA-IMF Large Program (cite: Motte22) and is motivated by previous observations of top-heavy CMFs (cite: Motte18b; Pouteau22a).

evidence.quote: The molecular cloud complex W43, located at 5.5 kpc from the Sun (cite: zhang14) at the junction point of the Scutum-Centaurus spiral arm and the galactic bar, is known as a particularly active star-forming region.

question.value: Compare populations of protostellar and prestellar cores in W43-MM1, W43-MM2, and W43-MM3 to understand the origin of the top-heavy core mass functions (CMFs) and core mass growth.

evidence.quote: We aim to compare populations of protostellar and prestellar cores in three regions imaged in the ALMA-IMF Large Program.

In this work, we aim to further discriminate protostellar and prestellar cores using outflow detections, in order to address the question of the origin of the top-heavy CMFs measured by (cite: Motte18b) and (cite: Pouteau22a).

Observations of W43-MM1 at 1.3 mm (Band 6) were carried out in Cycle 2 between July 2014 and June 2015 (project #2013.1.01365.S), with the ALMA 12-m array covering baselines ranging from 7.6 m to 1045 m.
This paper makes use of the ALMA data ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.01355.L.

CO (2–1) cubes of W43-MM2&MM3 were also processed using the ALMA-IMF data pipeline, although without self-calibration (see (cite: Cunningham23) for more detail on line data reduction).

analysis_steps.goal: Denoise continuum maps and extract core catalogues

method.value: Apply MnGSeg wavelet denoising to continuum maps, run getsf using denoised bsens/bsens* for detection and denoised bsens/bsens* and cleanest for flux and size measurements, apply post-selection filters, and replace contaminated fluxes with cleanest measurements for hot cores.

evidence.quote: In short, the denoising process relies on MnGSeg (cite: Robitaille19), a wavelet-based method which decomposes an image into a Gaussian component associated with the cloud structure and the noise and a coherent component containing the hierarchical star-forming structures.

Following the approach developed by (cite: Pouteau22a) towards W43-MM2&MM3 (see 2.2.1), we performed the source extraction with getsf using the denoised $\texttt{bsens}^*$ image for the detection step and the denoised $\texttt{bsens}^*$ and cleanest images for measurements.

key_parameters.value: Post-selection filters: size < 4x beam, ellipticity < 2, peak and integrated flux S/N > 2; flux ratio threshold > 3 sigma for hot core line contamination correction in W43-MM1

evidence.quote: The catalogue of the combined regions contains 208 sources passing the recommended post-selection filters (i.e. size lower than four times the beam, ellipticity lower than 2, peak and integrated flux signal-to-noise ratios above 2).

analysis_steps.goal: Identify protostellar and prestellar cores via molecular outflows and hot core emission

method.value: Visually inspect CO (2-1) cubes channel by channel and integrated high- and low-velocity wing maps to identify outflow lobes associated with cores, supplement with hot core emission surveys, and classify cores without either signature as prestellar candidates.

evidence.quote: Cores with neither outflows nor hot core emission are classified as prestellar candidates.
The identification of outflow lobes has been done through a detailed inspection of the CO cube.

key_parameters.value: Outflow lobe detection threshold: > 5 sigma in 3 consecutive channels; V_LSR = 92 km s^-1; high-velocity windows: 53.6-61.2 and 119.6-127.2 (or 125.9-133.6) km s^-1; low-velocity windows: 73.9-75.1 and 110.7-112.0 km s^-1

claims.hypothesis: The top-heavy global Core Mass Function (CMF) in W43 is driven by the protostellar core population rather than a top-heavy prestellar core population.
claims.experiment: Classify cores in W43-MM1 and W43-MM2&MM3 into protostellar and prestellar populations using CO (2-1) outflows and hot core emission, and fit their separate CMFs above the 1.6 M_sun completeness limit using MLE and bootstrap methods.
claims.result: The prestellar CMF high-mass slope is alpha = -1.46 (+0.12/-0.19), consistent with the Salpeter slope (-1.35), while the protostellar CMF is flat/top-heavy with alpha = -0.64 (+0.09/-0.07) and the protostellar fraction rises from 15-20% at 0.8-3 M_sun to 80% above 16 M_sun.
claims.finding: The prestellar CMF in W43 is Salpeter-like and the top-heavy character of the global CMF is caused by the protostellar core population.

evidence.quote: Our analysis also revealed that the high-mass slope of the prestellar CMF in W43, $\alpha=-1.46_{-0.19}^{+0.12}$, is consistent with the Salpeter slope, and thus the top-heavy form measured for the global CMF, $\alpha=-0.96 \pm 0.09$, is due to the protostellar core population.

claims.hypothesis: Cores grow in mass during the protostellar phase via inflow from their environment (clump-fed scenario), with mass growth rates increasing with core mass.
claims.experiment: Compare the median masses, maximum masses, and CMF slopes of prestellar and protostellar core populations in W43 under the assumption of ergodicity.
claims.result: Protostellar cores have a higher median mass (8.9 M_sun vs 2.7 M_sun), extend to higher maximum mass (109 M_sun vs 37 M_sun), and have a significantly flatter CMF slope than prestellar cores.
claims.finding: Cores gain mass during the protostellar phase at a rate exceeding outflow/accretion mass loss, supporting clump-fed models where high-mass cores accrete more strongly than low-mass cores.

evidence.loc: Mass distribution of prestellar and protostellar cores
evidence.quote: In detail, the median deconvolved sizes and masses of protostellar cores are 1800 au and 8.9$\,\ensuremath{M_{\odot}}$, respectively, while those of prestellar cores are 2600 au and 2.7$\,\ensuremath{M_{\odot}}$.

The existence of protostellar cores more massive than prestellar cores thus implies that cores are able to grow in mass during the protostellar phase through inflow and accretion from their environment, which can be included in the previous equation with an additional term $\dot{M}_{\rm core}$:

In addition, the flattening of slope between the prestellar and protostellar CMFs implies that $\dot{M}_{\rm core}$ depends on the core mass, and more precisely that high-mass cores are able to grow in mass more strongly than low-mass cores.

claims.hypothesis: The lower fraction of protostellar cores at low core masses is an observational artifact caused by CO (2-1) sensitivity limits.
claims.experiment: Measure the unambiguous channel-by-channel detection intensity S/N of the 18 outflow lobes driven by the lowest-mass protostellar cores (0.8-1.6 M_sun) in W43-MM2&MM3.
claims.result: Detection intensities of outflow lobes for 0.8-1.6 M_sun cores range from 5.7 sigma to 49 sigma with a median of 17 sigma, well above the 5 sigma detection threshold.
claims.finding: CO sensitivity is not limiting the detection of outflows from low-mass cores in W43, so the increase of protostellar fraction with core mass is not a sensitivity bias.

evidence.quote: Their detection intensity, excluding a lobe with confusion, range from 5.7$\sigma$ to 49$\sigma$, with a median of 17$\sigma$.
The result presented 3.3 that the fraction of cores which are protostellar decreases with mass is not due to a sensitivity limitation.

why_this_data.value: W43-MM1 and W43-MM2&MM3 are massive clumps in the active W43 star-forming complex where top-heavy global CMFs were previously measured; 12-m only data were chosen over 12-m + 7-m combined data because the combined data have higher noise without improving compact core or collimated outflow detection.

evidence.quote: In this work, we aim to further discriminate protostellar and prestellar cores using outflow detections, in order to address the question of the origin of the top-heavy CMFs measured by (cite: Motte18b) and (cite: Pouteau22a).

The combined 12-m + 7-m data indeed have higher noise levels than the 12-m only data (cite: Pouteau22a) without bringing information significant for this work, whether on the detection of compact cores or the identification of collimated outflows.

why_this_method.value: MnGSeg denoising reduces noise by ~30% and increases core detections without introducing spurious sources; getsf is suited for extracting compact cores in complex environments; molecular outflows in CO (2-1) and hot core emission are the primary and secondary signatures of the protostellar phase.

evidence.quote: (cite: Pouteau22a) showed that applying a "denoising" process on the continuum map before running the core extraction increases the number of detected cores thanks to an increased sensitivity, without introducing spurious sources or degrading the quality of flux measurements.
getsf is the successor of the sources and filaments extraction methods getsources and getfilaments (cite: Mensh12; Mensh13) and is well suited to extract compact cores in complex environments.

evidence.loc: Identification of protostellar cores using outflows
evidence.quote: Molecular outflows are the most common signature of the protostellar phase of cores in the millimetre wavelength range (cite: Bontemps96).

evidence.quote: Furthermore, this evaluation of cores gravitational boundedness should be considered with caution, as Bonnor-Ebert spheres are not the most appropriate models for the massive and dense cores in our observations.

limitations_admitted.value: The cumulative protostellar CMF of W43 is poorly represented by a single power-law across 1.6 to 109 M_sun.

evidence.quote: This result indicates that the protostellar CMF of W43, in its cumulative form, is poorly represented by a single power-law from 1.6 to 109 $\,\ensuremath{M_{\odot}}$.

limitations_admitted.value: W43-MM1 has a worse completeness limit (1.6 M_sun vs 0.8 M_sun) and stronger sidelobes than W43-MM2&MM3, which may produce more spurious low-mass prestellar core candidates below 1.6 M_sun.

evidence.quote: The continuum emission is more centrally concentrated and brighter in W43-MM1 compared to W43-MM2&MM3, which produces brighter sidelobes.
It likely prevents for good detections of weakest sources and possibly produces more spurious low-mass prestellar core candidates.

limitations_admitted.value: Outflow identification is relatively insensitive to low-velocity outflows (within ~10 km s^-1 of V_LSR) due to CO self-absorption and cloud contamination, and suffers from confusion in the dense central areas, making the number of protostellar cores a lower limit.

evidence.quote: First, we are relatively insensitive to outflows emitting only at low velocity, where the CO spectra suffer from strong self-absorption or contamination (about 10$\,\ensuremath{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$ from the central velocity, see 3).
We conclude that, although the number of detected protostellar cores is formally a lower limit, our outflow-based method does not introduce a significant bias as a function of core mass.

referee_caveats_inferred: Outflow identification and core attribution rely on visual inspection of CO (2-1) channel maps rather than an automated or reproducible algorithm.

Dust temperatures used to compute core masses are taken from lower-resolution maps (Motte et al. 2018b; Pouteau et al. 2022a) rather than measured at the 0.5'' core scale, which could bias the masses of internally heated protostellar cores vs externally heated prestellar cores.

Evolutionary interpretation of the prestellar-to-protostellar CMF flattening relies on the assumption of ergodicity, which the authors note may be violated if W43 is undergoing a time-dependent burst of star formation.
